candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — somatic symptom and related disorders
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate somatic symptom disorder from illness anxiety disorder, factitious disorder, and malingering using symptom burden, excessive health concern, persistence, and intentionality/external incentive.

options.A: Malingering, which involves intentional symptom production for an external incentive
options.B: Factitious disorder, which involves intentional falsification without an obvious external reward
options.C: Illness anxiety disorder, which is characterized by preoccupation with serious illness despite absent or only mild somatic symptoms
options.D: Somatic symptom disorder, which involves distressing symptoms plus excessive symptom-related thoughts, feelings, or behaviors

candidate.rationale: Somatic symptom disorder requires one or more distressing somatic symptoms that cause significant disruption, excessive symptom-related thoughts, feelings, or behaviors, and persistence of the symptomatic state, typically for more than 6 months. The symptoms do not have to be medically unexplained and are not intentionally fabricated. D is therefore the only option that matches the complete pattern.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Somatic symptom disorder includes distressing/disruptive somatic symptoms, excessive symptom-related thoughts/feelings/behaviors, and persistent symptomatic status typically longer than 6 months; symptoms may or may not be medically explained.

candidate.stem: For more than 6 months, a client has had one or more distressing physical symptoms that disrupt daily life and are accompanied by persistent excessive health-related thoughts, anxiety, and time devoted to the symptoms. Which disorder is most consistent with this presentation?
